annotations.title: The Key Independence Fact
annotations.content: The heart of Wald's Identity: X_{k+1} is independent of {τ > k}, because {τ > k} ∈ ℱ_k (stopping time condition) while X_{k+1} is independent of ℱ_k (i.i.d. property). This allows factoring E[X_{k+1} · 1_{τ>k}] = E[X_{k+1}] · P(τ > k).

annotations.title: Conditional Expectation Pull-Out
annotations.content: The proof uses the pull-out property E[fg | m] = f · E[g | m] when f is m-measurable (condExp_mul_of_stronglyMeasurable_left). Combined with E[X_{k+1} | ℱ_k] = E[X_{k+1}] from i.i.d. independence, this yields the factorization.

annotations.title: Tail Sum Formula
annotations.content: The formula E[τ] = ∑_{k≥0} P(τ > k) is the discrete analogue of E[X] = ∫₀^∞ P(X > t) dt (layer cake). For ℕ-valued τ: (τ ω : ℝ) = ∑' k, 1_{k < τ ω} as a finite sum that telescopes to τ ω.

annotations.title: Comparison with Optional Stopping Theorem
annotations.content: While the OST (proved in FairGamesTheoremOQ02OQ01) computes E[X_τ] for a stopped martingale, Wald's Identity computes E[∑_{k≤τ} X_k] for a stopped SUM of i.i.d. variables. They complement each other: OST handles the endpoint, Wald handles the path sum.
